newsitem.title: ITALY: Generali profits slip as lira climbs.
newsitem.headline: Generali profits slip as lira climbs.

text.p: Italy's largest insurer Generali on Thursday reported a 11.7 percent fall in first half 1996 profits as it suffered from a stronger lira but Europe's number two insurer said 1996 could still be better than 1995.
The insurance giant, based in the Italian north eastern city of Trieste, said parent company first half 1996 pretax profits slipped to 516 billion lire ($340.9 million) from 584.6 billion.
Generali added its ordinary operating profits had risen in the first half by 120 billion lire, but the appreciation of the Italian currency had wiped some 204 billion lire off profits.
Analysts said that the first half results were in line with forecasts and they still saw full year 1996 parent company net profits ahead of the previous year.

"The results were in line with our forecasts but we are awaiting further details surrounding the exchange losses," said an analyst at a Milan brokerage house. No-one was available to comment on the figures at Generali's headquarters in Trieste.
The analyst was sticking to his parent company net profit of 518 billion lire for 1996 after 482 billion lire in 1995.
The company said that its results for 1996 could be between than those reported in 1995 in the absence of unforeseen events affected its insurance business.
The results were announced just before the Milan stock market closed and Generali shares finished up 1.55 percent at 31,568 lire in a generally firmer share market.

The insurer, second only to German Allianz in Europe, said its total premium income rose 8.2 percent to 5.56 trillion lire with life premiums up 17.5 percent and non-life business increasing by 1.2 percent.
The company made solid progress in Italy with life premiums up 8.5 percent and non-life business 6.6 percent ahead.
Analysts said that the group's consolidated results for the whole of 1996 would gain after it sold its stake in French insurer AXA in September for around 1.75 trillion lire. ($ = 1513 Italian Lire)
